operations.exact_original_value: **Input and framing convention.** Let h be one four-dimensional one-handle attached compatibly to an oriented four-dimensional stage, with feet in a connected compact oriented three-dimensional base N. The stage orientation makes the normal bundle of each closed core orientable; its rank-three frame can be closed as in [F2]. Let B and B′ be two embedded replacement arcs joining its feet, with framed product tubes and the same parametrized germs at their endpoints. They avoid every other one-handle foot and the protected boundary collar. A finite system of framed two-handle attaching curves may traverse h any number of times, with either orientation. Apply the explicit cancellation/routing construction with either arc. Its links are $R_B(L)\cup U\qquad\hbox{and}\qquad R_{B'}(L)\cup U.$ Here U may be chosen as the same small zero-framed circle in both diagrams: take its cross-section on the common endpoint germ. Its disk meets each routed strip once for each signed traversal of h. Its framing is the product disk framing. This convention follows by transporting the meridian along the product cancellation tube; it fixes the actual exterior marking. Assume first that B and B′ have disjoint interiors outside their common endpoint germs. No restriction is placed on the homotopy class of their union. The two framed arc strips, with oppositely oriented common germs, join to a framed embedded ribbon annulus about a closed curve K that follows B′ and returns along a parallel of B. More precisely separate the strips by distinct normal coordinates, cut both just inside their common germs, and join the four short ends by the two planar rectangles in the endpoint balls. The core of the resulting annulus is K. Its annular normal is the integer framing used below. This choice records any difference in twisting of the two replacement arc framings; no independently chosen integer is substituted.
